graph/description: **The black-hole mass spectrum:** how many detected mergers have their heavier mass in each log-spaced bin. It is not one smooth slope: a pile near $10\,M_\odot$, a second bump near $35\,M_\odot$, then a tail running straight through the pair-instability gap (purple), where no black hole born from a single star should be. The heavy ones may be *second-generation*: remnants of earlier mergers, paired again in dense star clusters. Caveat: these are detected counts. A merger is heard out to a distance that grows with its chirp mass, roughly $d \propto \mathcal{M}^{5/6}$, so the volume searched grows as $\mathcal{M}^{5/2}$ and heavy mergers are strongly over-represented; the true population has relatively far more light ones (the GWTC population papers correct for this).
graph/name: The black-hole mass spectrum: two peaks and a tenanted gap
